egc-sizing.formula: EGC size from NEC Table 250.122, keyed to the upstream OCP rating; min size driven by OCP, parallel runs sized per NEC 250.122(F).
egc-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
egc-sizing.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Conductor material
assumptions.value: user-selectable; copper default

phase-balance.formula: Per-phase totals, then imbalance % = (max - min) / average x 100. The swap suggestion is a greedy pass that moves the largest circuit that fits under half the gap from the heaviest phase to the lightest. The spread (max - min) / average is about twice NEMA's maximum-deviation-from-average measure (48/52/50 A: 8% here, 4% by NEMA).
phase-balance.edition: Engineering practice; NEC Article 220 by name.
phase-balance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
phase-balance.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

egc-upsize-proportional.formula: ratio = max(1, installed_phase_cmil / base_phase_cmil); upsized_EGC_cmil = base_EGC_cmil x ratio, then select the next standard AWG/kcmil at or above this. A ratio below 1 is clamped to 1 (the EGC is never reduced below its table size).
egc-upsize-proportional.edition: NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). 250.122(B) (increase in size of equipment grounding conductors).
egc-upsize-proportional.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
egc-upsize-proportional.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: User-supplied tables
assumptions.value: the base EGC size (from the 250.122 table for the OCPD) and the minimum-required phase area are user-supplied; the tile bundles neither table

assumptions.name: Upper bound
assumptions.value: the EGC need never exceed the ungrounded conductors it runs with; the AHJ governs the final size

refrigerant-line-size.formula: area_ft2 = (mass_flow_lb_hr * specific_volume_ft3_lb) / (60 * target_velocity_fpm); line ID_in = 12 * sqrt(4 * area / pi). The inverse of the line-velocity relation, solved for the diameter that meets the oil-return minimum velocity.
refrigerant-line-size.edition: ASHRAE Refrigeration Handbook line-sizing and oil-return guidance, by name.
refrigerant-line-size.freeAccess: ASHRAE licensed; refrigerant specific volume is read from the manufacturer's P-T / property data (user-supplied).
refrigerant-line-size.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
refrigerant-line-size.editionNote: The inverse of refrigerant-velocity: the largest line inside diameter that still meets the oil-return minimum velocity (about 1500 fpm in a suction riser, 700 fpm horizontal). A line at or below this ID keeps the refrigerant fast enough to sweep oil back; a larger line traps oil, and a smaller line raises the pressure drop. Single-edition; the oil-return minimums are advisory and manufacturer-table-governed.

assumptions.name: Oil-return window
assumptions.value: horizontal min ~700 fpm, suction-riser min ~1500 fpm (advisory)

assumptions.name: Specific volume
assumptions.value: refrigerant specific volume at the line condition is state-specific and user-supplied

stairs.formula: Riser height and tread depth from total rise / number of risers; IRC 2021 §R311.7.5 residential limits 7-3/4″ max riser, 10″ min tread (the 7″ / 11″ pair is the commercial IBC §1011.5.2 rule).
stairs.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
stairs.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IRC 2021. Jurisdictions on IRC 2018 / 2024 differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Standard riser max
assumptions.value: 7-3/4 in residential per IRC §R311.7.5.1

assumptions.name: Standard tread min
assumptions.value: 10 in residential per IRC §R311.7.5.2

rent-vs-buy.formula: discount d_t = 1/(1+i)^t, i = investment return. PV_buy = down_payment + Σ ownership_outflow_t * d_t − net_sale * d_N, where ownership_outflow_t = P&I x (months of year t still inside the loan term) + tax_pct*price + insurance + HOA*12 + maint_pct*price and net_sale = price*(1+appr)^N − sell_pct*value − loan_balance_N. PV_rent = Σ rent*12*(1+rent_infl)^(t-1) * d_t. difference = PV_buy − PV_rent.
rent-vs-buy.edition: New York Times 'Is It Better to Rent or Buy?' rent-vs-buy methodology (published interactive). AICPA personal-financial-planning guidance. First-principles discounted cash flow.
rent-vs-buy.freeAccess: The NYT methodology is published; the DCF math is universal. CFPB homebuyer materials free at consumerfinance.gov.
rent-vs-buy.governance: Estimate. Lender governs final underwriting and rate / fee disclosure. Appraiser governs the appraised value. State law and the agency's program guidelines may impose stricter limits than the published thresholds.
rent-vs-buy.editionNote: Estimate only. Tax treatment (mortgage-interest deduction, SALT cap, the Section 121 capital-gains exclusion) is out of scope and materially changes the answer; consult a CPA. Property tax, insurance, HOA, and maintenance are held at the entered values (not inflated) for transparency. The down payment's opportunity cost is captured by discounting at the investment-return rate, so the renter's retained down payment correctly carries zero net present value.

assumptions.name: Discount rate
assumptions.value: the investment-return rate is used as the opportunity cost of capital for both paths

assumptions.name: Annual cash flows
assumptions.value: ownership and rent outflows discounted at year-end; mid-year timing not modeled

periodic-element.formula: Lookup table over atomic number, symbol, or name. Returns period / group / block / Pauling electronegativity / electron configuration / common oxidation states.
periodic-element.edition: IUPAC atomic numbers and element names (current IUPAC). Pauling electronegativity per Pauling, 'The Nature of the Chemical Bond' (3rd ed., 1960). Electron configurations per NIST Atomic Spectra Database. Common oxidation states per Greenwood + Earnshaw, 'Chemistry of the Elements' (2nd ed., 1997); Cotton + Wilkinson, 'Advanced Inorganic Chemistry'.
periodic-element.freeAccess: NIST Atomic Spectra Database free at physics.nist.gov/asd. IUPAC nomenclature free at iupac.org.
periodic-element.governance: Estimate only. Readability formulas and similar metrics are derived from a representative population and have known edge-case noise. The classroom teacher governs final text selection, grade placement, and assessment decisions.
periodic-element.editionNote: Coverage is the first 36 elements (H through Kr) plus Ag, I, Au, Hg, Pb. The full table (118 elements) would add ~2 KB; that is a future extension. Pauling electronegativity is undefined for the noble gases (the tile returns 'noble gas; not defined' for He / Ne / Ar). The Kr Pauling value is included where defined.

assumptions.name: Coverage
assumptions.value: H-Kr plus 5 selected heavy elements; full table out of scope for this Y.12 extension

assumptions.name: Electronegativity scale
assumptions.value: Pauling scale; Allred-Rochow and Mulliken scales are alternatives

curve-deflection-stakeout.formula: deflection from the back tangent at the PC: delta = (l / (2R)) x (180/pi) deg for an arc length l; sub-chord from the PC c = 2R sin(l / (2R)); arc-definition D = 5729.58 / R. The deflection at the PT equals half the curve's total central angle.
curve-deflection-stakeout.edition: Deflection-angle curve-stakeout method per FM 5-233 Construction Surveying and the AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (the Green Book), by name; first-principles trig.
curve-deflection-stakeout.freeAccess: FM 5-233 is public-domain US Government work, free at US Army publication archives. The design of record and the engineer of record govern the alignment.
curve-deflection-stakeout.governance: Estimate. Engineer of record governs the design and acceptance. Verify against the project structural drawings and the manufacturer's published capacity / chart.
curve-deflection-stakeout.editionNote: Single-edition (first-principles curve trig). The deflection-angle method sets each station by turning the running-total deflection from the back tangent and pulling the sub-chord; the deflection at the PT closes on half the total central angle. Simple circular curve only - no spiral (transition) or superelevation.

assumptions.name: Degree definition
assumptions.value: arc definition D = 5729.58 / R

assumptions.name: Reference
assumptions.value: deflection measured from the back tangent at the PC; chord is the straight sub-chord from the PC

map-scale-conversion.formula: ft_per_inch = representative_fraction / 12; ground_distance_ft = map_distance_in x ft_per_inch; acres_per_sq_inch = ft_per_inch^2 / 43,560; ground_area_acres = map_area_sqin x acres_per_sq_inch.
map-scale-conversion.edition: Representative fraction to ground units, with area scaling as the SQUARE of the linear scale, by name; public map arithmetic. The 1:24,000 USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle at 2,000 ft per inch is named as the familiar case, not reproduced from any table. The map's own scale bar, its datum, and a GIS measurement govern anything that matters.
map-scale-conversion.freeAccess: Multiplication and division on the map's stated scale and the user's own measurements.
map-scale-conversion.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
map-scale-conversion.editionNote: A representative fraction of one to twenty-four thousand means one unit on the map is twenty-four thousand of the same units on the ground, and because the fraction is unitless the conversion to feet per inch is a division by twelve. That is where the familiar two thousand feet to the inch on a standard quadrangle comes from, and with it the old rule about an inch being roughly a third of a mile. Area is where map arithmetic goes wrong, because scale enters area squared. A map at twice the scale denominator does not cover twice the ground per square inch, it covers four times, so a square inch on a small-scale sheet is worth many times what it is worth on a quadrangle -- a factor of seventeen between the two most common US sheet scales, for a linear scale only about four times smaller. Anyone estimating a burn area, a search segment, or a parcel off a map without squaring the scale will be off by a large multiple, and the error always runs toward underestimating the smaller-scale sheet. The acres-per-square-inch output exists so that the squaring is done once, visibly, rather than assumed.

assumptions.name: Unitless fraction
assumptions.value: RF / 12 gives ground feet per map inch directly

assumptions.name: Area is squared
assumptions.value: ground per square inch goes as the SQUARE of the linear scale; 43,560 sq ft per acre

assumptions.name: Paper and datum
assumptions.value: the map's own scale bar governs; paper distortion and the sheet's datum are not modeled

belt-conveyor-tension-power.formula: material load Wm = tph x 2000 / (speed x 60); friction = f x L x (2 Wb + Wm + Wrot); lift = H x Wm; Te = friction + lift; belt hp = Te x speed / 33,000; motor hp = belt hp / drive efficiency.
belt-conveyor-tension-power.edition: The simplified CEMA effective-tension form with the belt counted on both the carrying and return sides, and belt horsepower = Te x speed / 33,000, by name; the friction factor (about 0.022 for a well-maintained conveyor) and the idler rotating weight are entered rather than tabulated. Effective tension and drive power only. CEMA's Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials, the belt and idler manufacturers, and the engineer of record govern.
belt-conveyor-tension-power.freeAccess: The simplified effective-tension form is stated and cited to CEMA rather than reproduced from it; every weight and factor is user-entered.
belt-conveyor-tension-power.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
belt-conveyor-tension-power.editionNote: Effective tension is the force the drive pulley must deliver, and it is the sum of two physically different things. The friction term is everything resisting motion along the run -- the belt counted on both the carrying and return sides, the material, and the rotating mass of the idlers -- times a friction factor and the length. The lift term is the potential energy being added, and it is the material weight per foot times the rise. Nothing else. Which term dominates decides what to fix, and that is the entire reason for printing them separately rather than as one number. On a short steep conveyor the lift term can be several times the friction term, and no amount of maintenance touches it: perfect idlers save a fraction of a horsepower where halving the rise saves several, so a marginal motor is a profile problem. Reverse the geometry to a long flat run at the same tonnage and the friction term becomes everything, at which point idler condition, alignment, and belt tension are the whole conversation. What this does not do is size the conveyor. It computes no tension distribution around the loop, no slack-side tension to prevent drive-pulley slip or belt sag between idlers, and no take-up travel, and it selects no belt carcass, ply, cover, or splice. Acceleration, braking, and the runaway condition on a declining conveyor are separate and important problems of their own.

assumptions.name: The belt counts twice
assumptions.value: carrying and return sides both appear in the friction term
assumptions.source: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials

assumptions.name: Which term dominates sets the lever
assumptions.value: lift-dominated means the profile; friction-dominated means idlers and alignment
assumptions.source: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials

assumptions.name: Not a conveyor design
assumptions.value: no tension distribution, slack side, take-up, belt selection, acceleration, or braking
assumptions.source: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials

rock-construction-entrance.formula: volume_cy = length_ft x width_ft x (depth_in/12) / 27; tons = length_ft x width_ft x (depth_in/12) x unit_wt_pcf / 2000.
rock-construction-entrance.edition: Pad take-off identity by name (length x width x depth x unit weight); first-principles volume arithmetic.
rock-construction-entrance.freeAccess: The pad take-off is public quantity-survey geometry; the pad dimensions come from the general permit or AHJ.
rock-construction-entrance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rock-construction-entrance.editionNote: The general permit or AHJ sets the pad dimensions - commonly at least 50 ft long, the full width of the exit, and 6 in of 1-4 in clean stone over a geotextile separator. The geotextile under the pad is taken off separately. The pad is topped up as it works into the subgrade.

assumptions.name: Pad dimensions
assumptions.value: 50 ft x 14 ft x 6 in default (>= 50 ft long, full exit width); the general permit / AHJ governs

assumptions.name: Stone
assumptions.value: 1-4 in clean stone at ~100 pcf placed over a geotextile separator (taken off separately)

hose-lay-section-count.formula: lay_length_ft = map_distance_ft x (1 + slack_fraction); sections = ceil(lay_length_ft / section_length_ft); actual_reach_ft = sections x section_length_ft; gal_per_ft = pi x (hose_id_in/2)^2 x 12 / 231; charged_weight_lb = sections x (dry_weight + gal_per_ft x section_length x 8.34).
hose-lay-section-count.edition: Hose lay section count as a ceiling function on the map distance padded by a slack allowance, with the charged weight from the hose's internal volume at 8.34 lb per gallon, by name. Public geometry. The actual approach, department SOPs, and the officer on the line govern.
hose-lay-section-count.freeAccess: The volume and count arithmetic is public geometry. The distance, slack allowance, section length, hose size, and dry weight are the department's own values.
hose-lay-section-count.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
hose-lay-section-count.editionNote: The section count is a ceiling function on a padded distance, and both halves of that matter. A hose lay never runs the straight-line distance on the map: it goes around the building, up the stairs, and over the fence, so a slack allowance of about a fifth is a conservative planning figure that a bad approach will exceed. Undercounting by a single section at the end of a long lay is a break in the line at the worst possible moment, which is the whole reason a lay is counted before it is pulled rather than discovered short while it is being advanced. On a long approach the difference between what the map says and what the ground takes can be several sections. The weight line is the one crews feel rather than calculate. Water is 8.34 pounds per gallon and a two-and-a-half-inch line holds about a quarter gallon per foot, so a fifty-foot section carries roughly a hundred pounds of water on top of the hose itself and a long lay is more than a ton of charged line. That is manageable while it is moving on flat ground and effectively immovable the moment it has to be advanced up a stairwell, which is the number behind every rule about advancing dry and charging at the door.

assumptions.name: Slack allowance
assumptions.value: about 20% is a conservative planning figure; a bad approach exceeds it

assumptions.name: Hose volume
assumptions.value: pi (d/2)^2 x 12 / 231 gallons per foot, at 8.34 lb per gallon

assumptions.name: Count before pulling
assumptions.value: one section short at the end of a long lay is a break in the line at the worst moment

pipe-insulation-takeoff.formula: cut_ft = pipe_ft x (1 + waste_pct/100) + num_fittings x fitting_allow_ft; sections = ceil(cut_ft / section_len_ft); jacket_sf = PI x (insul_od_in/12) x cut_ft.
pipe-insulation-takeoff.edition: Mechanical-insulation takeoff identity by name (cut length with fitting allowances; sections and jacket from the cut); first-principles takeoff arithmetic.
pipe-insulation-takeoff.freeAccess: The takeoff is public quantity-survey arithmetic; the insulation thickness and jacket type come from the mechanical specification.
pipe-insulation-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pipe-insulation-takeoff.editionNote: The fitting allowance covers ells, tees, and valves (a valve is several feet of equivalent length). The jacket area uses the insulation outside diameter (not the pipe). This is a material takeoff distinct from the thermal insulation-thickness; the spec sets the thickness and jacket type.

assumptions.name: Fitting allowance
assumptions.value: insulation length per ell/tee/valve (~1 ft default; a valve is several feet)

assumptions.name: Jacket diameter
assumptions.value: the insulation outside diameter (pipe OD + 2 x thickness), not the pipe

log-limb-weight.formula: volume = (pi/3) x length x (r1^2 + r1 r2 + r2^2) with r = dia/24 (frustum; cylinder when butt = top); weight = volume x green density.
log-limb-weight.edition: USDA Forest Products Laboratory Technical Note 218, Weights of Various Woods Grown in the United States (green column); first-principles frustum volume.
log-limb-weight.freeAccess: FPL Technical Note 218 is free at fpl.fs.usda.gov (US government). The frustum volume is public geometry.
log-limb-weight.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
log-limb-weight.editionNote: Green density varies with species, moisture, and season; the bundled values are FPL Technical Note 218's green weights, which it cautions can be off by as much as 20% - weigh or conservatively over-estimate. A tapered frustum is lighter than a cylinder of the butt diameter, so a cylinder estimate is the safe side. This is the static load that tree-rigging-shock multiplies.

assumptions.name: Green density
assumptions.value: TN-218 green weights (red oak 63, coast Douglas-fir 38, slash pine 56, eastern white pine 36, etc., lb/ft^3); generic hardwood 58 and softwood 45 are round figures

tree-open-cavity.formula: hollow_d = D - 2t; R = min(1, opening_width / (pi x D)); closed_loss = (hollow_d^3 / D^3) x 100; open_loss = (hollow_d^3 + R x (D^3 - hollow_d^3)) / D^3 x 100.
tree-open-cavity.edition: Smiley & Fraedrich (1992) open-cavity strength-loss formula, by name.
tree-open-cavity.freeAccess: The Smiley & Fraedrich open-cavity relation is published arboriculture research (ISA Arboriculture & Urban Forestry); a qualified arborist governs the assessment.
tree-open-cavity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
tree-open-cavity.editionNote: R is the cavity opening's arc as a fraction of the circumference - an open face makes the ring a broken tube, far weaker than a closed hollow. The formula collapses to Wagener's cube law when the opening closes. It can underestimate a large cavity with a deep wedge and a thick sound wall, so use it with caution there. The ISA 33% strength-loss guide is a common concern trigger, not a failure prediction. A qualified arborist and an ISA TRAQ assessment govern - a screen, not a load rating.

assumptions.name: Opening ratio
assumptions.value: R = opening arc / circumference; the opening adds R of the remaining sound wood (D^3 - hollow_d^3) to the loss

assumptions.name: Collapses to Wagener
assumptions.value: at R = 0 (closed hollow) the formula equals the Wagener (hollow_d/D)^3 loss

bearing-equivalent-load.edition: The ISO 281 dynamic equivalent load P = X Fr + Y Fa with the standard single-row deep-groove ball-bearing X/Y/e table vs Fa/C0 (ISO 281; SKF General Catalogue; Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design), by name; feeds the bearing-l10-life and bearing-max-load tiles.
bearing-equivalent-load.freeAccess: The equivalent-load relation and the deep-groove ball X/Y/e table are published ISO 281 / catalogue data; the radial and thrust loads and the static rating C0 come from the application and the bearing catalog.
bearing-equivalent-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bearing-equivalent-load.editionNote: The ISO 281 dynamic equivalent load for a single-row deep-groove ball bearing, P = X Fr + Y Fa, the input the bearing-l10-life and bearing-max-load tiles need but do not compute. The thrust factor Y and the e-ratio are interpolated from the standard ISO 281 / SKF table on Fa/C0, C0 the basic static load rating. If the thrust-to-radial ratio Fa/Fr is at or below e the pure radial load governs (X = 1, Y = 0, so P = Fr); above e the bearing carries the thrust as extra equivalent load with X = 0.56 and the interpolated Y. With Fa = 0 the result is exactly P = Fr, which feeds bearing-l10-life directly. Single-row radial deep-groove ball bearings, rotating inner ring (V = 1); angular-contact, tapered-, and spherical-roller bearings use the maker's bearing-specific factors. A planning estimate; ISO 281 and the bearing maker's catalogue govern.

assumptions.name: Equivalent load
assumptions.value: P = X Fr + Y Fa; X = 0.56 for Fa/Fr > e, else X = 1 and Y = 0

assumptions.name: X/Y/e table
assumptions.value: single-row deep-groove ball, e and Y interpolated on Fa/C0 over the 12 published rows (0.014->0.56)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: deep-groove ball, rotating inner ring V = 1; other bearing types use maker factors

carbon-equivalent.formula: CE = C + (Mn + Si)/6 + (Cr + Mo + V)/5 + (Ni + Cu)/15 (AWS D1.1 Annex XI; Si = 0 gives the IIW form). Bands: < 0.35 readily weldable; 0.35-0.55 preheat advised; > 0.55 high hardenability.
carbon-equivalent.edition: AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code (2000) Annex XI carbon equivalent, which adds Si to the IIW formula, by name; published formula.
carbon-equivalent.freeAccess: Published weighted-sum formula; the output is a screening band, not a qualified welding procedure.
carbon-equivalent.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
carbon-equivalent.editionNote: The IIW / AWS D1.1 carbon-equivalent weighted sum. This is a screen, not a welding procedure; the WPS, hydrogen level, restraint, and thickness govern the actual preheat (AWS D1.1 Annex).

assumptions.name: Composition
assumptions.value: the steel chemistry (weight percent of C, Mn, Si, Cr, Mo, V, Ni, Cu) is user-supplied from the mill certificate

vehicle-road-load-power.formula: F_total = 1/2 rho V^2 Cd A + Crr W + W sin(atan(grade%/100)); P = F_total V; hp = F_total V / 550. Aero term from aerodynamic-drag-force.
vehicle-road-load-power.edition: The vehicle road-load equation (aerodynamic drag + rolling resistance + grade) and the tractive power (SAE J2263 / J1263 coastdown road-load), by name; the aero term is delegated to aerodynamic-drag-force.
vehicle-road-load-power.freeAccess: The road-load equation is a standard published vehicle-dynamics result; the drag coefficient, frontal area, rolling coefficient, weight, and grade are the user's inputs.
vehicle-road-load-power.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
vehicle-road-load-power.editionNote: Steady-speed vehicle road load: the tractive force is aero drag F_aero = 1/2 rho V^2 Cd A (delegated to the aerodynamic-drag-force tile) plus rolling resistance F_roll = Crr W plus the grade load F_grade = W sin(atan(grade%/100)), and the power to hold the speed is P = F_total V. Rolling resistance is nearly constant with speed (Crr ~ 0.010-0.015 on pavement); aero grows with the square of speed and its power with the cube; grade adds a fixed pull of the weight times the slope. The three-way breakdown shows which dominates - at highway speed on the level the wind leads, but even a modest grade quickly takes over. This is the power AT THE WHEELS; divide by the driveline efficiency for engine/motor power, and add the mass x acceleration term for launch. Headwind and air-density change with altitude/temperature are separate. A planning estimate; the manufacturer's coastdown road-load data governs.

assumptions.name: Road load
assumptions.value: F_total = aero + Crr W + W sin(atan(grade%/100)); P = F_total V

assumptions.name: Aero delegation
assumptions.value: aero term computed by aerodynamic-drag-force (no drift)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: steady speed at the wheels; acceleration, driveline efficiency, headwind are separate

main-disinfection-chlorine.formula: volume_gal = 0.0408 x diameter_in^2 x length_ft; available_cl_lb = (volume / 1,000,000) x dose_mg/L x 8.34; product_lb = available_cl / (weight % / 100) for a dry product; liquid_gal = available_cl / (8.34 x trade % / 100) for a liquid labeled in trade percent.
main-disinfection-chlorine.edition: AWWA C651 Disinfecting Water Mains (by name).
main-disinfection-chlorine.freeAccess: AWWA C651 licensed; the dose/contact-time methods are public water-works practice.
main-disinfection-chlorine.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
main-disinfection-chlorine.editionNote: Single-edition (the standard and the local health authority govern; the AHJ is the law).

assumptions.name: Dose / contact time
assumptions.value: continuous feed at least 25 mg/L with 10 mg/L left after 24 hours; slug at least 100 mg/L for at least 3 hours, rechlorinated if it drops below 50 mg/L

assumptions.name: Product strength
assumptions.value: cal-hypo (HTH-type) is roughly 65 to 70% available chlorine; liquid sodium hypochlorite is the label trade %

assumptions.name: Clearance
assumptions.value: flush and pass a bacteriological test, and dechlorinate any chlorinated water before discharge

water-heater-storage-sizing.formula: recovery_gph = input_btuh x efficiency/100 / (8.33 x rise_F); first-hour rating FHR_gph = tank_gal x usable_fraction + recovery_gph; the verdict compares FHR to the peak-hour demand.
water-heater-storage-sizing.edition: First-principles recovery Q = 8.33 x gph x delta-T with the DOE/AHRI first-hour-rating definition (usable storage plus one hour of recovery), by name, not reproduced.
water-heater-storage-sizing.freeAccess: The recovery relation is public physics; the DOE/AHRI first-hour-rating test value on the EnergyGuide label and the manufacturer govern the rating.
water-heater-storage-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
water-heater-storage-sizing.editionNote: Single-edition (the manufacturer's rated first-hour rating on the DOE EnergyGuide label and the AHJ govern the selection).

assumptions.name: Constants
assumptions.value: the default 0.70 usable-storage fraction (before the stored water drops below the set point) is editable; the 8.33 lb/gal water constant is fixed

assumptions.name: FHR definition
assumptions.value: first-hour rating = usable storage + one hour of recovery; match it to the peak-hour draw, not to tank gallons alone

assumptions.name: Check, not rating
assumptions.value: this is a sizing check; the manufacturer's tested FHR on the yellow EnergyGuide label is the governing value

battery-c-rate.formula: c_rate_power_kw = nameplate_kwh x c_rate; deliverable_kw = inverter_kw > 0 ? min(c_rate_power_kw, inverter_kw) : c_rate_power_kw; usable_kwh = nameplate_kwh x dod; discharge_time_h = usable_kwh / deliverable_kw.
battery-c-rate.edition: The standard battery C-rate definition (power = nameplate x C, full discharge time = 1 / C, deliverable power = the lesser of the C-rate power and the inverter rating), by name; the relations are public.
battery-c-rate.freeAccess: The C-rate definition and the power/duration arithmetic are public; manufacturer discharge-rate data is published in cut sheets.
battery-c-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
battery-c-rate.editionNote: The battery C-rate definition (power = nameplate x C, full discharge time = 1 / C, and the deliverable power is the lesser of the C-rate power and the inverter rating, with an inverter rating of zero meaning no inverter limit). The continuous C-rate is the sustained rating, not the brief surge rating (a pack delivers more for seconds than for an hour); the usable energy uses the depth of discharge; high discharge rates lose a few points of capacity and add heat. A nameplate power check, not a cell-level thermal model.

assumptions.name: C-rate power
assumptions.value: continuous power = nameplate energy x C-rate (0.5C = half the nameplate energy per hour)

assumptions.name: Deliverable power
assumptions.value: the lesser of the C-rate power and the inverter/PCS continuous rating (0 = no inverter limit)

assumptions.name: Discharge time
assumptions.value: usable energy (nameplate x DoD) divided by the deliverable power

thermal-stress-restrained.formula: sigma = E alpha dT x restraint; F = sigma A; free_delta = alpha L dT.
thermal-stress-restrained.edition: The standard restrained thermal-stress relation (mechanics of materials), by name.
thermal-stress-restrained.freeAccess: The restrained thermal-stress relation is published free in any mechanics-of-materials reference. The engineer of record governs the design.
thermal-stress-restrained.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
thermal-stress-restrained.editionNote: Restrained thermal stress: a member blocked from expanding develops sigma = E x alpha x dT x restraint (independent of length), and the restraint force F = sigma x A. Heating a restrained member puts it in compression; cooling puts it in tension. The free (unrestrained) expansion alpha x L x dT is the movement the restraint blocks. Aluminum's larger expansion coefficient but lower modulus can net a lower thermal stress than steel. This returns the stress and force for the entered restraint factor: fully restrained (factor 1) is the worst case, and real supports give partial restraint; it does not check member buckling under the induced compression. A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Restrained stress
assumptions.value: sigma = E alpha dT x restraint, independent of length

assumptions.name: Sign
assumptions.value: heating a restrained member -> compression; cooling -> tension

assumptions.name: No buckling check
assumptions.value: fully restrained is the worst case; buckling under the compression is not checked

boussinesq-surcharge-wall.edition: The NAVFAC DM-7.2 modified-Boussinesq line-load lateral pressure on a rigid wall, the doubled elastic Boussinesq solution for an unyielding wall, by name.
boussinesq-surcharge-wall.freeAccess: NAVFAC DM-7.2 is public-domain and free online; the modified-Boussinesq surcharge relations are public.
boussinesq-surcharge-wall.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
boussinesq-surcharge-wall.editionNote: The NAVFAC DM-7.2 modified-Boussinesq line-load lateral pressure sigma_h = (0.20 qL/H) n/(0.16 + n^2)^2 for m <= 0.4 and (1.28 qL/H)(m^2 n)/(m^2 + n^2)^2 for m > 0.4, the doubling of the elastic Boussinesq solution for an unyielding (non-deflecting) rigid wall, and m = x/H, n = z/H. This returns the lateral pressure at a single depth from a line load parallel to the wall - it uses the rigid-wall (doubled) form (a flexible wall that can deflect sees roughly the un-doubled Boussinesq value), covers a line load (a point or strip load uses the companion NAVFAC forms), and does not integrate the resultant thrust and its point of application or add the at-rest/active earth pressure beneath it. A design aid, not a substitute for the geotechnical engineer of record's report.

assumptions.name: Modified Boussinesq
assumptions.value: the two m-branch forms with m = x/H, n = z/H; doubled for a rigid non-deflecting wall

assumptions.name: Line load
assumptions.value: a load per unit length parallel to the wall; point/strip loads use the companion forms

assumptions.name: Single depth
assumptions.value: pressure at one z; the integrated resultant thrust is a separate step

injector-max-hp.formula: inj_lbh = flow (or cc/min / 10.5); total_lbh = inj_lbh x n_cyl x duty; hp_max = total_lbh / BSFC.
injector-max-hp.edition: The fuel-injector-sizing relation solved for the supported power, the inverse of the injector-size tile, a standard tuning-reference result, by name.
injector-max-hp.freeAccess: The injector-sizing relation and the BSFC ranges are public results in the engine-tuning references.
injector-max-hp.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
injector-max-hp.editionNote: The maximum horsepower a fuel-injector set supports, the inverse of the injector-sizing tile: HP_max = injector lb/h x n_cyl x duty / BSFC, the fuel the injectors can flow at a safe maximum duty cycle divided by the brake-specific fuel consumption. The injector static flow is entered in lb/h or cc/min (lb/h x 10.5 = cc/min for gasoline, SG ~0.72). Because BSFC rises with boost and richer tuning (~0.45-0.50 NA to ~0.55-0.65 boosted), the same injectors support meaningfully less power once boost richens the tune; the customary maximum duty cycle is 80% (headroom above that risks a lean fuel cut at redline). It assumes evenly-distributed port injection with one injector per cylinder, and does not cover a return-versus-returnless fuel system, the rail pressure that sets the static flow, or direct injection. A tuning aid; the engine's measured fueling and the tuner's judgment govern.

assumptions.name: Power capacity
assumptions.value: hp_max = injector lb/h x n_cyl x duty / BSFC

assumptions.name: BSFC
assumptions.value: ~0.50 naturally-aspirated gas, 0.55-0.65 boosted; entered by the user

assumptions.name: Conversion
assumptions.value: lb/h x 10.5 = cc/min for gasoline (SG ~0.72); 80% max duty

bolt-shear-bearing.formula: Rn_shear = ns x Fnv x Ab; bearing/tearout Rn = min(1.2 lc t Fu, 2.4 d t Fu) with lc = le - dh/2 (edge) or s - dh (interior); governing = min; phi Rn = 0.75 Rn; Rn/Omega = Rn/2.00.
bolt-shear-bearing.edition: AISC 360-22 §J3.7 (Table J3.2 Fnv) and §J3.11, by name; the material Fu and the bolt Ab / Fnv are standard tabulated values.
bolt-shear-bearing.freeAccess: The bolt shear-rupture and bearing / tearout relations and their phi / Omega factors are stated in AISC 360 §J3; the Fnv values are in Table J3.2.
bolt-shear-bearing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bolt-shear-bearing.editionNote: AISC 360-22 §J3.7 bolt shear rupture Rn = nplanes x Fnv x Ab (Fnv from Table J3.2: 54 ksi A325-N, 68 ksi A325-X, 68 ksi A490-N, 84 ksi A490-X) and §J3.11 bearing / tearout at a bolt hole Rn = 1.2 lc t Fu <= 2.4 d t Fu, where lc is the clear distance in the line of force (edge bolt: le - dh/2; interior bolt: s - dh). The governing per-bolt nominal strength is the smaller of bolt shear and edge bearing / tearout; the design strength is phi x Rn (phi = 0.75) and the allowable is Rn / Omega (Omega = 2.00). Standard holes and the deformation-considered coefficients; one bolt at one hole (group action, slip-critical, and combined tension-shear are separate checks). A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Two limit states
assumptions.value: the per-bolt strength is the smaller of shear rupture (Fnv Ab) and bearing / tearout (1.2 lc t Fu, capped at 2.4 d t Fu)

assumptions.name: Clear distance lc
assumptions.value: edge bolt lc = le - dh/2; interior bolt lc = s - dh, in the line of the force

assumptions.name: Factors
assumptions.value: phi = 0.75 (LRFD) and Omega = 2.00 (ASD); standard holes, one bolt at one hole

building-tightness-limit.formula: the ASHRAE 62.2 whole-house requirement 0.03 x floor area + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1) in cfm, converted to a CFM50 tightness limit by multiplying by the LBL N-factor; the house is below the limit when its measured CFM50 falls under it, and the margin is the sealing that can be done before mechanical ventilation is required.
building-tightness-limit.edition: ASHRAE 62.2 whole-house ventilation by name, with the LBL N-factor conversion between natural and 50 Pa flows. The limit is a SCREEN on whether air sealing will drive a house below its ventilation requirement, not a substitute for the 62.2 calculation or for a measured ventilation rate.
building-tightness-limit.freeAccess: One published rate expression and one divisor.
building-tightness-limit.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
building-tightness-limit.editionNote: This is the number that decides whether an air-sealing scope needs a ventilation fan in it, and the reason to run it BEFORE the work rather than after: a house 7% above the limit is one afternoon of sealing away from needing a fan, and finding that out afterwards is an expensive way to learn it. Natural infiltration credited against the requirement is a seasonal average and is wrong on any given day by a wide margin, which is why current practice is increasingly to ventilate mechanically and treat infiltration as an energy term only.

assumptions.name: Infiltration credit is a seasonal average
assumptions.value: wrong on any given day by a wide margin

assumptions.name: N-factor
assumptions.value: climate zone, height and shielding; a threefold range

assumptions.name: Not a signed test report
assumptions.value: a screen, not a rater's certification

machinery-room-ventilation.formula: required emergency exhaust Q = 100 x sqrt(G) in cfm for A1 refrigerants, with G the mass in pounds of the largest single system's charge, or 30 air changes per hour on the gross room volume for ammonia (IIAR 2); air changes = Q x 60 / room volume; louver free area = Q / face velocity, and the gross louver is that over the free-area fraction; the charge an installed fan covers is (cfm/100) squared.
machinery-room-ventilation.edition: The emergency mechanical ventilation rate as ANSI/ASHRAE 15 states it for A1 refrigerants, and IIAR 2 (2014, 2021 6.14.7.1) at 30 air changes per hour for ammonia, which ASHRAE 15 has excluded since 15-2016 Addendum a. A2L rooms (ASHRAE 15-2022 Table 8-3) are not computed. Louver face velocity and free-area fraction are ENTERED (louver-free-area relates them). It does not size the separate continuous ventilation rate for occupied heat removal, set refrigerant-detector locations or setpoints, evaluate the discharge location, or determine whether a machinery room is required.
machinery-room-ventilation.freeAccess: One square root and one area; no standard text is reproduced.
machinery-room-ventilation.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
machinery-room-ventilation.editionNote: Two features of the relation carry the engineering. The square root means doubling the charge multiplies the requirement by about 1.41 rather than 2, because the rate dilutes a credible release to a survivable concentration rather than handling the entire charge. And it is the LARGEST SINGLE SYSTEM that governs rather than the sum in the room, because the design event is one system failing. The number that actually fails inspections is makeup air: a large exhaust fan in a tight room depressurizes it, rides up its curve, and delivers a fraction of the design. Detection is the other half -- ventilation that has to be started by a person already overcome is not a safety system.

assumptions.name: Louver face velocity and free area are entered
assumptions.value: they depend on the louver selected and its pressure drop

assumptions.name: The continuous rate is separate
assumptions.value: occupied heat removal is a different and much smaller requirement

assumptions.name: Detection is not computed
assumptions.value: the detector, its setpoint and the alarm are part of the same design

stacking-aisle-width.formula: Right-angle stacking aisle = outside turning radius + load length along the forks + load face to turning centre + operating clearance; the turret / VNA case reduces to load length + clearance; module pitch = 2 x rack row depth + aisle.
stacking-aisle-width.edition: Truck manufacturer right-angle stack data at the actual load and mast, and the fire code's aisle requirements as adopted.
stacking-aisle-width.freeAccess: The geometry is public; right-angle stack figures come from each truck manufacturer's published specification sheet.
stacking-aisle-width.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
stacking-aisle-width.editionNote: The three truck types differ only in where the load sits relative to the turning centre. A narrow aisle is bought with guidance, a superflat floor tolerance, tighter rack alignment, slower aisle entry, and one truck per aisle.

assumptions.name: Truck dimensions
assumptions.value: entered per type; a manufacturer's right-angle stack figure at the actual load and mast supersedes the build-up

assumptions.name: Module fit
assumptions.value: whole modules across the entered width; cross-aisles, columns, and egress are not deducted
